name: Rahab
bio:
Rahab was a prostitute in the city of Jericho who was spared, along with her entire family, when she hid Israel's spies and put her trust in Israel's God — making her one of the most unexpected examples of faith in Scripture, and her name later appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.

## 👤 Identity and Background: A Prostitute in Jericho

Joshua sent two men to secretly scout out Jericho, and they lodged at Rahab's house. When the king of Jericho learned of them and demanded she hand them over, Rahab hid them instead, telling his messengers the men had already left, and secretly sent them up to the roof, hidden among stalks of flax (Joshua 2:1-6).

## 📖 Core Story: Hiding the Spies and the Promise of Safety

1. **Declaring Faith in Israel's God**: Rahab told the two spies, "I know that the LORD has given this land to you... for we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you... and what you did to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites... for the LORD your God is God in heaven above and on earth below" (Joshua 2:9-11), showing that she had come to genuinely believe, from reports alone, that Israel's God ruled over all things.
2. **Securing a Covenant for Her Family**: Rahab made the spies swear that when the city was taken, they would spare her and her whole household; they agreed, instructing her to tie a scarlet cord in her window as a sign and to gather her entire family inside her house so they would be spared (Joshua 2:12-21).
3. **Lowering Them Down the Wall**: Because her house was built into the city wall, Rahab lowered the two men down by a rope through her window, allowing them to escape their pursuers safely and return to Joshua three days later (Joshua 2:15-23).

When Israel finally conquered Jericho and its walls fell, Joshua instructed the same two spies to bring Rahab and her father, mother, brothers, and all who belonged to her out of the city and settle them safely outside the Israelite camp (Joshua 6:22-25).

## ✨ Key Character and Theological Significance

- **A Model of Faith Among the Gentiles**: Rahab was by any ordinary standard the least likely person in Jericho to be chosen, yet her genuine faith in Israel's God saved her; the New Testament book of Hebrews lists her among the great examples of faith: "By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies, was not killed with those who were disobedient" (Hebrews 11:31), and James cites her as proof that true faith is always accompanied by action (James 2:25).
- **Grafted into the Lineage of Christ**: Rahab later married Salmon of the tribe of Judah and became the mother of Boaz and the great-great-grandmother of King David, so her name appears in the genealogy of Jesus Christ recorded in Matthew (Matthew 1:5) — a striking example of God's grace reaching across national and personal history.

Rahab's story reminds us that genuine faith has nothing to do with one's background — God's grace can reach anyone who truly turns to him, even writing their name permanently into the story of redemption.
